title: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, Is Today
summary: Diwali is the biggest festival of the year in India, and it falls today, November 8. More than one billion people celebrate it, in India and around the world. Its name comes from 'Deepavali,' which means 'a row of lights.' People put rows of small clay oil lamps outside their homes. The lights stand for good winning over evil, and learning over not knowing. Diwali follows the Hindu moon calendar, so it usually falls in late October or early November. Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists all mark the day. In southern India, people celebrate Lord Krishna's win over the demon Naraka. In northern India, they celebrate Lord Rama coming home with his wife, Sita, and his brother, Lakshmana, after 14 years in the forest. Families light lamps and fireworks, eat big meals, wear new clothes, and pray. Some people buy gold on Dhanteras, the first day of the festival, for good luck. In North America, Disney World in Florida had events with more than 500 dancers, and New York City marked its 11th year of Diwali at Times Square.
why_it_matters: Diwali shows you how families in your class or neighborhood may celebrate light, kindness, and learning with lamps and big meals.
